name: veterinary_clinic_system_073_provider_location_coverage
instruction: Produce the provider coverage and workload report for the org-admin staffing review, batched under the episode batch code in ops_reports. The providers table lists each team member's home location, but providers are frequently cross-booked to see patients at other locations — the appointment schedule is the source of truth for where work happened, not the provider's home. Create one ops_reports row per location with report='provider_coverage': {batch_code, location_id, location_name, veterinarians (count of providers with role='veterinarian' at that location), support_staff (count of providers with any other role at that location), total_providers, has_kennel_staff (true iff at least one provider at that location has role='kennel_attendant'), active_patients (patients with status='active' at that location), patients_per_veterinarian (round(active_patients/veterinarians, 1) if veterinarians > 0 else 0.0), appointments_at_location (appointments with location_id=this location), completed_at_location, no_show_at_location, completed_pct (round(100*completed_at_location/appointments_at_location, 1) if any), no_show_pct, total_runs (boarding_runs at this location), occupied_runs, occupancy_pct (round(100*occupied_runs/total_runs, 1) if total_runs else 0.0)}. Then create one ops_reports row per provider with report='provider_workload': {batch_code, provider_id, provider_name, role, location_id (home location), home_location_name, appointment_count (appointments with provider_id=this provider, regardless of appointment location), completed_count, no_show_count, completion_pct (round(100*completed_count/appointment_count, 1) if any), no_show_pct (round(100*no_show_count/appointment_count, 1) if any)}. Include every provider, even those with zero appointments. No collection outside ops_reports may be modified.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Recompute per-location coverage (vets, support, kennel staff, active patients, appointments, occupancy) and per-provider workload (appointments, completed, no-show, percentages) from live data; exactly one provider_coverage row per location and one provider_workload row per provider. Every aggregate verified by both a raw-row Python pass and an independent SQL pass.

checks.expect: per-location and per-provider appointment counts and rates computed by raw-row filter and SQL agree with each other and the written rows

hazards: Provider home location is not the appointment location: 364 of 548 appointments have a provider whose location_id differs from the appointment's location_id (e.g. appointment id=1 is at location 1 with provider_id=3, whose home is location 2). Using provider home location for appointment counts produces wrong coverage and workload numbers.

Support staff (roles 'vet_tech', 'kennel_attendant', 'groomer') all have zero appointments in the schedule (providers id=5, 6, 7, 8, 9). They must still appear in provider_workload with appointment_count=0 and in provider_coverage as support_staff; an agent that filters to providers with appointments drops them.

Location 2 has no provider with role 'kennel_attendant' (Lucy Tran is a groomer at loc 2), so has_kennel_staff is false only for location 2; an agent that treats any non-veterinarian as kennel staff gets this wrong.

patients_per_veterinarian is computed from active_patients at the location (loc 1: 100 active / 2 vets = 50.0, loc 2: 106 / 1 = 106.0, loc 3: 93 / 1 = 93.0). An agent that counts all patients or all providers gets a different ratio.

The appointment status mix is not uniform per location: loc 1 has 187 appointments (58 completed, 27 no_show), loc 2 has 181 (58 completed, 20 no_show), loc 3 has 180 (60 completed, 19 no_show). These counts must come from appointments.location_id, not providers.location_id.
